text.en: Prabhat could not bear to lose, not even at marbles. He thought winning was everything. Then he met a new boy who lost a match and still laughed. This story shows how watching someone else made Prabhat change his heart about games. Let us see how.

Think about the games you play for fun and the games you play for competition, and how you feel when you win or lose. Four words to know: friendly matches are games played without serious competition, an opponent is someone you compete against, a tally of marks is a record of points in a game, and sporting spirit means being fair and respecting every player.
Prabhat always wanted to win. His parents, teachers and friends said he did not know how to accept defeat. He could not bear losing even at marbles. Winning made him feel great and losing made him feel terrible, as if it was the worst thing that could happen. If he sensed he would lose a game, he would not play it. He took part only when sure of winning, and he only played games he was good at, such as badminton.
A new student named Surya joined the school and was an excellent badminton player. Prabhat waited for the last Friday of the month, when the coach organised friendly matches in the games period. Teams were decided on Monday, and Prabhat and Surya were chosen to play against each other. Prabhat was given the job of keeping the score. He prepared very seriously, but Surya seemed relaxed, smiling and joking all week.
On Friday Surya was a real phenomenon, which means a person with special qualities. He won point after point while laughing and joking. But he was paying so little attention that Prabhat managed to change the scoreboard while his opponent was looking elsewhere. So Prabhat won by cheating and made a big thing of his win. It did not matter to Surya, who said it had been fun and that they should play again some time.
Everyone was talking about how well Prabhat had played, yet he could not sleep that night. He had won but did not feel as happy as usual. He was surprised that Surya did not feel bad about losing. The next day he was more surprised to see Surya playing basketball so badly that he could not score for ten minutes, yet still enjoying himself. His feeling that night was unhappiness, because deep down he knew he had cheated.
Prabhat watched Surya closely for some days. Surya was great at some things and terrible at others, but he enjoyed everything equally. Prabhat realised that to enjoy a game you do not need a scoreboard or worry about winning or losing. You need to enjoy the game for its own sake and just try to do well. He changed himself. He began playing hide and seek and felt sad when it ended, and he even joked while playing badminton. Soon the other students said that Prabhat was good fun to play with and had a great sporting spirit. That is why the title Change of Heart fits the story.
Past perfect tense shows the first, older action when two things happened in the past. It is formed with had plus the third form of the verb. In the sentence Everyone was discussing how Prabhat had played so well, had played is the older action and was discussing is the newer one. Practice: Prabhat had already finished his homework before going to the match. Surya had played basketball for years before joining the badminton team. By the time Prabhat arrived, Surya had already won several matches. Surya had never met Prabhat before coming to the school, and Prabhat had practised extensively before the games period.

To request, say could you please. To apologise say I am sorry, that was my fault. To thank, say I truly appreciate your help. Sportspersons from India such as Deepika Kumari, who practised with bamboo bows and won gold at the 2010 Commonwealth Games, and Neeraj Chopra, the javelin Olympic gold medallist, show hard work and spirit.

problem.en: Fill in with the past perfect: Prabhat ____ already ____ his homework before going to the match. (finish)

text.en: Past perfect needs had plus the third form of the verb.

why.en: The finishing happened before going to the match.

text.en: So the sentence is: Prabhat had already finished his homework before going to the match.

why.en: Finished is the third form of finish.

problem.en: Find words hidden in PHENOMENON in order.

text.en: Look at consecutive letters without changing their order.

why.en: You may only take letters side by side.

text.en: You can find hen, no, men, omen and non.

prompt.en: Explain how Prabhat changed and why the title Change of Heart suits the story.

requiredIdeas.en: He felt unhappy even after winning.
He saw Surya enjoy games without worrying about winning.
He learnt to enjoy the game for its own sake and showed sporting spirit.

commonMisconceptions.en: Prabhat won the badminton match fairly.

points.en: Change of Heart is a story about Prabhat and Surya.
Prabhat could not bear losing and cheated in a badminton match.
He felt unhappy and learnt from Surya to enjoy games for their own sake.
Sporting spirit means being fair and respecting all players.
Past perfect uses had plus the third form to show the earlier action.
Please, thank you and sorry are three magic words.
